title: Insecticide for Rice Bug (Atangya): What Works and When to Spray
metaTitle: Insecticide for Rice Bug: What Works and When to Spray
metaDescription: The insecticide for rice bug most Philippine labels name is lambda cyhalothrin. See what else is registered, when a spray pays, and how to time it right.
excerpt: The insecticide for rice bug that most Philippine labels name is lambda cyhalothrin, a pyrethroid. Cypermethrin, malathion, thiamethoxam and the mix of lambda cyhalothrin with thiamethoxam are registered for it on rice too. But a spray only pays when your count passes the threshold during flowering to the milky stage. Count first, spray late in the afternoon if you must, and always follow the label of an FPA registered product.

blocks.text:
Farmers often ask for the gamot sa atangya, the one product that stops the rice bug for good. The answer has two parts. Several insecticides on Philippine labels work on it. But the timing and the count decide whether any of them is worth the money.

The rice bug, called atangya or alitangya in Tagalog, sucks the grain while it is still milky. So the danger window is short, from flowering to the soft dough stage. A spray before or after that window is wasted, and a spray inside it without a count may kill the spiders and wasps that were already keeping the bugs down.
When an insecticide for rice bug pays
Count before you buy anything. Walk the field early in the morning or late in the afternoon, when the bugs rest on the panicles. Then compare your count with these signs.

blocks.caption: When to consider control of the rice bug
rows: More than 5 nymphs and adults per square meter
More than 10 nymphs and adults per square meter

blocks.text: Below these numbers, let natural enemies do the work. Small wasps grow inside rice bug eggs, and long horned grasshoppers and spiders eat the eggs and young bugs. Our guide on [when to spray rice pests](/blog/when-to-spray-rice-pests) lines these counts up with the other rice pests.
Active ingredients registered for rice bug in the Philippines

These are the active ingredients whose Philippine labels name the rice bug on rice, most common first. Pick a product whose FPA registered label lists rice bug on rice, and read that label for the rate.

blocks.text: Rotate groups from one spray to the next. Lambda cyhalothrin followed by cypermethrin counts as the same group, and bugs that live through the first spray may live through the second. Our guides to [Karate, Cymbush and Selecron](/blog/karate-cymbush-selecron-insecticides) and to [Alika, Virtako and Chess](/blog/rice-insecticides-alika-virtako-chess) compare the brands. Some popular sprays, such as Goldrush, are registered on rice for planthoppers, leafhoppers, black bug, leaffolder and stem borer. Their labels do not name the rice bug, so check the label before you buy.
How to time and apply the spray

items.title: Spray inside the window
items.text: Rice bugs feed from flowering to the soft dough stage. A spray before the panicles come out, or after the grain hardens, misses them.

items.title: Spray late in the afternoon
items.text: The bugs hide from the midday heat and come back to the panicles toward evening. Late afternoon also keeps the spray off the flowers that open in the morning.

items.title: Check the weather first
items.text: Rain within a few hours can wash the spray off the panicles, so look at the forecast for your lot before you mix.

items.title: Start at the field edges
items.text: Rice bugs move in from the grasses on the levees and canals, so the edges often hold the most.

items.title: Respect the days before harvest
items.text: The bug feeds close to harvest, so the pre harvest interval on the label matters. Never spray inside it.

items.title: Wear protection
items.text: Use gloves, long sleeves, a mask and boots, as the label says. Wash after spraying, and keep children and animals away.

blocks.title: Do not spray just because you saw a few bugs
blocks.text: A spray without a count kills the wasps and spiders that hold rice bugs and planthoppers down. Then the pests come back stronger, and the next spray has to be bigger.

items: **Cut the grasses** on the pilapil and the canals before the crop flowers, since the bugs live on them between seasons.
**Plant with your neighbors.** Fields that flower at the same time share the bugs, instead of feeding one wave after another.
**Sweep with a net** at dawn or dusk in small fields.
**Use bait.** Rotting snails or fish hung on sticks draw the bugs to one spot, where you can kill them.
**Keep natural enemies** by skipping early sprays you do not need.
**Pick awned varieties** where you can, since the awns hold the bugs off.

blocks.text: Questions about the insecticide for rice bug

items.q: What is the best insecticide for rice bug?
items.a: Lambda cyhalothrin is the active ingredient most Philippine labels name for rice bug on rice, and cypermethrin, malathion and thiamethoxam are registered too. The best choice is a product whose FPA registered label lists rice bug on rice, sprayed only when your count passes the threshold.

Ang pinakakaraniwang sangkap sa mga label para sa atangya ay lambda cyhalothrin. Pero gamitin lang ito kapag mataas na ang bilang ng atangya mula pamumulaklak hanggang paggatas ng butil, at sundin ang label ng produktong rehistrado sa FPA.

items.q: When should I spray for rice bug?
items.a: Only from flowering to the soft dough stage, only when the count passes the threshold, and late in the afternoon when the bugs are back on the panicles.

items.q: Can I use Goldrush for rice bug?
items.a: Its label names planthoppers, leafhoppers, black bug, leaffolder and stem borer on rice, but not the rice bug. Use a product whose label names the rice bug, or ask your technician.

items.q: How many days before harvest can I spray?
items.a: It depends on the product. Read the pre harvest interval on its label, and never spray inside it.

items.q: Do I need to spray for rice bug every season?
items.a: No. Many seasons stay below the threshold, especially when the whole area plants together and the grasses around the fields are cut.
